name: Week 25 Legs — The RDL Plate Finally Moves (Spotlight: Bulgarian + Leg Press)
description:
**Warmups are baked into each block's notes as a reminder.**

**The incline RDL steps to 55 (45 + a 10).** It's been at the same plate for months and always reported back hard — until last week, when you went *slower* than prescribed to compensate and it still didn't burn. The tempo lever is spent, so the load moves. Keep stacking and come back down if it bites too hard.

**Two new machines join as maintenance: hip abduction and adduction.** They run as one station pair, 2 sets each. The leg press stays at 4 sets — a set on a machine you're already standing at costs almost nothing; it's the walking and waiting that eats the session.

**Leg curl fallback is written in** in case that machine is still broken.

dayOverview.theme: Two changes. The incline RDL's plate moves for the first time in months — the tempo lever got pushed harder than prescribed last week and the lift still didn't respond, which is the program's own escalation order arriving at step two. And the hip abduction/adduction pair joins as light maintenance — added on top rather than traded against anything, since the cost of a session is stations walked to, not sets performed. Everything else holds, including the squat at 80, which produced its best ROM to date on bad sleep.

spotlights.why: It threw up something worth chasing: the right leg — normally the stronger one — was dying from the first rep as the front leg, and it felt like trunk rather than quad. You noted it only ever shows up here, which isn't as strange as it sounds. The Bulgarian is the only lift on this day that is genuinely single-leg with the rear foot elevated; squats, leg press and calf raise are all bilateral or supported, so they hide frontal-plane stability. This is the only test that asks the question. So the spotlight is on holding a level pelvis, not on the load.

It read 'deep and felt easy and good' last week at the same four plates that felt 'way harder' the week before, and the only thing that changed was the day. That makes it a good spotlight precisely because there's no problem to solve — the attention can go to what actually makes a leg press work, which is depth. Knees toward the chest, judged by range rather than by burn. Four sets, full range on every one of them — including the fourth, which is where depth usually quietly shortens.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Legs spotlights: W24 squat + incline RDL · W25 Bulgarian + leg press (current) · W26 leg curl + calf raise · W27 squat depth returns. Hip abduction/adduction enter as maintenance this week — they're not spotlight material, they're insurance.
watchpoints: **🔆 Incline RDL steps to 55 (45 plate + a 10).** Keep the 3s eccentric and the 2s bottom pause. **Stack up and come back down if it bites** 🛑.

**🔆 Bulgarian: watch the RIGHT front leg.** It died from rep one last week on the side that's normally stronger, and it felt like trunk more than quad. **Level pelvis is the cue** — don't let the hip on the rear-leg side drop 🛑.
**🔆 Leg press: 4 plates, 4 sets** 🔥. Full depth every rep — judge the range, not the burn.

**NEW: hip abduction + adduction machines, 2 sets each**, run as one station pair. **Maintenance, not progression** — abduction is the one that matters here; it's the pelvis-leveling muscle the Bulgarian exposes.
**Adductor machine: log the number, don't distrust it.** It reads very high (~315 in W8) — that's the machine's stack ratio, not a fault.
**Squat holds 80/side, 3 working sets**, ramp 45 → 70 🛑. Best ROM to date last week, on bad sleep. Brace from the ramp.

**Leg curl: back seat at POSITION 5, pyramid 90 → 100 → 110** 🔥. **If the machine is still broken:** Nordic curl, eccentric-only, 3 × 3-5 — it's the only knee flexion in the program. Extra hip-machine sets fill the time but not the function.
**Calf raise stays on the leg press** — same machine, same 4 plates, slow eccentric and hold the bottom stretch 🔥.
**Intensity tags:** 🔥 near-failure last set OK — leg press, calf raise, leg curl, hip abduction/adduction. 🛑 keep it shy — squat, Bulgarian, incline RDL, Nordic.
**Take the stations as they come free.** The order below is the ideal grouping, not a rule.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release + Dead-Bug Core/QL Primer)
sets.notes: The dead bug is the brace rehearsal for the squat — same ribs-down, low-back-flat position, unloaded.

exercises.notes: Full depth, easy pace — find the range before it's loaded.
30s each side. QL release — give it the full beat.
Open the hips, both directions.
Shins — knee insurance.
Spinal warmup.
Hinged slightly forward, tight fists, thumbs tucked.
**Core/QL primer, and the brace rehearsal for today.** Ribs DOWN, low back flat to the floor — that contact is the same brace the squat wants.
Bodyweight, controlled — last thing before the ramp.

sets.name: Squat Warmup — the ROM Ramp (45 → 70), Brace Rehearsal 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 45 for round 1, 70 for round 2, 8 reps each.

**This is where the brace gets set, not where you find out how the day is going.** The 45 feeling heavy predicts nothing — it felt awful two weeks ago and the 80s were the best of the day.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45 then 70.
- **Big breath into the belly, ribs DOWN**, brace before the descent
- **Hold the brace through the bottom** — don't let it go at the turnaround
- Full depth on every warmup rep — this is where the range gets set for the working sets

sets.name: Squat Working (80 × 3 Sets — Depth + Brace) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 80/side, 3 working sets of 6-8, full depth.

Best ROM to date last week on bad sleep, three sets of 8, slow and controlled. Same load, same job.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 80/side, 3 sets.
- **Breathe IN and brace before every descent**, hold it through the bottom
- **Depth over speed** — slow and controlled is what produced last week's range
- **Knees track the toes**, chest stays up out of the hole
- Catcher bars at 14 as the depth reference and the safety 🛑

sets.name: 🔆 Bulgarian Split Squat (Spotlight — Level Pelvis) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** Smith machine @45 + bench. **Double-50 DBs when the Smith is busy** — which it has been three weeks running.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the trunk, not the quad:**
- **Keep the pelvis LEVEL.** In single-leg stance the hip on the rear-leg side wants to drop; holding it up is glute medius, QL and obliques, and that's almost certainly what you felt as 'core not just legs'
- **The front leg does the work.** The rear foot is balance only
- **Front shin honest** — knee travels forward over the foot, don't shorten the range to keep it vertical
- **Ribs down, don't lean into the working side**
- **Watch the RIGHT leg specifically** — it was dying from rep one last week as the front leg, on the side that's normally stronger

**Reflection:** does the right still fade from the first rep, or was that one bad day? And can you feel whether the pelvis is staying level, or is it dropping and you're compensating with a lean?

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** Smith @45 + bench · double-50 DBs when the Smith is busy. Log which you used. Pigeon stretch between sets.

sets.name: 🔆 Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine — Deep ROM) 🔥
sets.notes:
**Both lifts on the same machine — don't leave the station between them.**

Leg press stays at 4 sets. Calf raise runs 3 on the same machine, so finish the leg press sets before switching.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side, 4 sets of 12.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — depth is the whole lift:**
- **Knees toward the chest on every rep** — judge the range, not the burn. The burn arrives either way; the range is what you're actually training
- **Feet mid-platform**, knees tracking the toes
- **Low back stays on the pad** — if the pelvis tucks at the bottom, you've gone past your range, not gained range
- **Slow eccentric**, don't drop into the bottom
- Don't lock the knees out at the top

🔥 Last set can go near failure.

**Reflection:** it read 'deep and easy' last week and 'way harder' the week before at the same plates. Which is it today — and does the depth hold through the fourth set, or does it quietly shorten?

**LOAD:** 4 plates/side, 3 sets of 15 (after the leg press's 4). **Stay on the leg press — same machine.**
- **Full stretch at the bottom, HOLD a beat** — don't bounce
- **Slow eccentric** all the way down
- Push through the balls of the feet, full extension at the top

🔥 Near-failure OK on the last set.

sets.name: Hip Abduction + Adduction (New — Maintenance Pair) 🔥
sets.notes:
**NEW this week. 2 sets each, run as one station pair — they usually sit next to each other.**

**If the leg curl is broken, run extra sets here instead** — you're already at the station and the machines are free. Just know it fills the time, not the function: these are hip work, and the hamstring's knee-flexion job still needs the Nordic.

**This is maintenance, not a progression surface.** Abduction is the one carrying the reason: it trains the muscle that levels the pelvis in single-leg stance, which is exactly what the Bulgarian exposes and what nothing else in the program directly loads. Adduction rides along — the cossacks and lateral lunges already cover most of it.

**On the numbers:** the adductor machine reads very high (~315 last time it was used). That's the machine's stack and pulley ratio, not a fault. **Log the number and move on.**

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** find it — start moderate and work up until the last few reps are honest.
- **Sit tall, don't lean back** to get more range
- **Push the legs apart slowly**, pause at the widest point
- **Control the return** — most of the value is in resisting the way back in
- Feel it on the outside of the hip, not the low back

🔥 Near-failure fine. **Log the number so there's a baseline.**

**LOAD:** find it. **The stack reads high on this machine (~315) — that's normal for it.**
- **Squeeze the legs together slowly**, pause at the top
- **Control the opening** — the stretch at the bottom is the useful part
- Sit tall, don't round the low back into it

🔥 Near-failure fine. **Log the number.**

sets.name: Seated Leg Curl (Back Seat at 5 — 90 → 100 → 110) 🔥
sets.notes:
**SETUP:** back seat at **position 5** — more leverage on the ankle, more natural. Ankles under the pad.

**LOAD:** **90 → 100 → 110** ascending, one set each.

**IF THE MACHINE IS STILL BROKEN:** do **Nordic curls, eccentric-only, 3 sets of 3-5** instead. Feet anchored, body straight from knees to head, lower slowly, catch with the hands, push back up. **Don't rig a cable-and-strap substitute** — it can't load anywhere near enough to be worth the setup.

**Why not just skip it:** the hamstring has two jobs. The incline RDL and every hinge cover hip extension; this is the only knee flexion in the program. Losing it doesn't lose redundant volume, it loses a whole function.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 90 → 100 → 110 ascending. Back seat at position 5.
- **Curl the heels all the way under the seat**, full range
- **Slow return**, don't let the stack pull you back
- Hips stay planted, no lifting off the seat to help

🔥 Near-failure OK on the 110 set.

**FALLBACK ONLY — if the leg curl machine is still broken.** 3 sets of 3-5, **eccentric-only**.
- Feet anchored, body straight from knees to head
- **Lower as slowly as you can control**, catch yourself with the hands
- Push back up with the arms — the way down is the whole exercise
🛑 Brutal, and it will make you sore the first time. Start with 3 reps.

sets.name: Incline RDL — the Plate Moves (55) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD: 55 — the 45lb plate plus a 10.** 3 sets of 12-15.

First load change on this lift in months. It reported back 'hard' or 'still burning' every single week until last week, when you went slower than prescribed to compensate and it still didn't burn. The tempo lever is spent, so the plate moves.

**Keep stacking if 55 is still easy; come back down if it bites too hard.** That's the method — the number is yours to adjust.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 55 (45 plate + 10). 3 sets.
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom** — the pause comes with you to the new weight
- **A hinge, not a bend** — hips go BACK, lower back stays neutral
- **Feel it in the hamstrings and glutes**, not the lumbar
- **Stop at neutral at the top** — no hyperextension
- Don't chase the floor with the plate; the hinge sets the depth

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)
sets.notes: Five minutes, mandatory. Hip and QL biased after a full legs day.

exercises.notes: 30s each side. QL downshift.
45s each side. Hips and glutes.
30s each side.
45s each side.
Slow breathing — parasympathetic shift.

tips: **Take the stations as they come free.** The order here is the ideal grouping, not a rule — the leg press and Smith get camped on.
**The RDL number is yours to adjust.** Stack up, come back down when it bites.
**Log which Bulgarian setup you used** — Smith @45 or double-50 DBs. They aren't the same lift.
